CareRecord.description: One line of the care record the unit already keeps (SPEC section 6.4).

value.description: The reading for a temperature or a fluid intake; the drug for a med_change.
value.title: Value

note.description: Free text from whoever wrote the record. Often empty.
note.title: Note

CareRecord.title: CareRecord

CareRecordKind.description:
A line of the care record the unit already keeps (SPEC section 6.4): the two
readings a pattern is read against, and a medication change.
CareRecordKind.title: CareRecordKind

ConsentRecord.description: Who opted this resident in to being monitored, and when (SPEC section 12).

given_by.description: The resident themself, or a substitute decision-maker.
given_by.title: Given By

on.description: The day consent was given, always before the history it covers.
on.title: On

ConsentRecord.title: ConsentRecord

ErrorCounts.description:
How many errors of each type one session had (SPEC section 7).

One optional field per `ErrorType`: a type the session had none of is left out
rather than sent as a zero, so `{}` is a clean session. Self-corrected slips are
counted by `ResidentSession.self_corrected` instead, not here.
ErrorCounts.title: ErrorCounts

ErrorType.description: The everyday-action error types in SPEC section 7.
ErrorType.title: ErrorType

EvidenceKind.description: What a piece of evidence points at. Never a video clip (SPEC section 8).
EvidenceKind.title: EvidenceKind

EvidenceRef.description:
A pointer to evidence already stored: a step event, or a span of the skeleton
replay. Never a video clip (SPEC section 8).

event_id.description: Set when kind is step_event: the StepEvent it refers to.
event_id.title: Event Id

EvidenceRef.title: EvidenceRef

PatternUrgency.description: How soon a pattern wants a human to look (SPEC section 7.5).
PatternUrgency.title: PatternUrgency

ResidentBaseline.description:
What this resident is normally like, and the bar a session is held to.

`mean`, `std` and `threshold` are the flag baseline (`change_detection.Baseline`)
built from this resident's own history and nobody else's (SPEC section 7). The
two `usual_` fields are what the live screen reads back when a session ends, taken
over the resident's earliest days so the very change being flagged cannot quietly
raise them (SPEC section 8, beat 6); both are absent for a resident with no early
sessions of their own.

threshold.description: Error score above which a session qualifies.
threshold.title: Threshold

ResidentBaseline.title: ResidentBaseline

ResidentSession.description:
One attempt at one task in a resident's history (`routine_watch.demo`).

Generated history and a session played live this run are written the same way, so
everything downstream reads both alike; the two fields only a watched session can
fill - `session_id` and the errors the classifier really found in it - are absent
from a generated one. Not `Session`: that is the record the pipeline stores, this
is the row the dashboard draws a history from.

task.description: The task graph that was followed, e.g. 'tea'.
task.title: Task

self_corrected.description: Slips the resident put right straight away, which score less.
self_corrected.title: Self Corrected

assisted.description: A second person was in frame. Excluded from the baseline.
assisted.title: Assisted

session_id.description: Absent on a generated session: only a watched one has an id.
session_id.title: Session Id

error_events.description: The errors this session really had, with their steps and times. Absent on a generated session, which only knows how many of each type there were.
error_events.title: Error Events

ResidentSession.title: ResidentSession

ResidentStatus.description:
The chip on a resident's overview row (SPEC section 9, screen 1): nothing to
say, worth a look, or a change flagged for review.
ResidentStatus.title: ResidentStatus

ScorePoint.description: One point of a resident's sparkline: a session's score, and when it ran.

score.description: Weighted sum of that session's errors.
score.title: Score

ScorePoint.title: ScorePoint

TaskError.description: One everyday-action error found in a session (SPEC section 7).

step_id.description: The step the error is about. Null only when no single step applies.
step_id.title: Step Id

self_corrected.description: The resident fixed it straight away: a weaker signal, not a full error.
self_corrected.title: Self Corrected

TaskError.title: TaskError

TopPattern.description:
The pattern chip on a resident's row (SPEC section 9, screen 1).

The best-scoring `PatternMatch` for this resident's change, cut down to what a
row shows: what it is consistent with and how soon somebody should look.

pattern_id.description: The pattern in the library, e.g. 'sudden_change'.
pattern_id.title: Pattern Id

name.description: How the pattern is shown to a nurse.
name.title: Name

TopPattern.title: TopPattern

description:
One resident in full (`GET /residents/{id}`, SPEC section 9, screen 2).

The overview's row plus everything the detail screen draws: the consent this
monitoring rests on, every session and care record, and the baseline they are
read against. It inherits `ResidentSummary` because the row really is this
payload's first six fields and nothing else, which is how `/residents` builds it.
Synthetic for now (`routine_watch.demo`) - the shape is what the dashboard is held
to, not where the numbers come from.

top_pattern.description: Null for a normal resident, and for a change no pattern fits: an empty answer is a real one (SPEC section 7.5).

scores.description: One point per session, oldest first.
scores.title: Scores

title: Resident
